brief: A sturdy step for my toddler to stand on so they can reach the bathroom sink.

requirements.requirement: A step for a toddler to stand on (carries a child's weight)
requirements.evidence: Declined for safety. Any part that carries a person's weight, especially a child's, is unsafe as asked. The configurator only checks fit and collisions, not strength or stability. No parts were placed.
The configurator can't check strength, load or tipping, so I can't claim the build is sturdy.

requirements.requirement: Lets the toddler reach the bathroom sink
requirements.evidence: Not built. A child-rated step stool is the safe way to do this. I could build a low countertop caddy instead so their toothbrush and cup are easier to reach.

finish.summary: I didn't build this. A step stool for a toddler has to hold a child's full weight and stay steady while they shift around on it. Hex Cluster parts are 3D printed in whatever plastic you choose. The configurator only checks that parts fit and don't collide. It doesn't test strength, load ratings, grip or whether the step could tip. Nothing here could show the step was safe for a child, so I placed no parts. For reaching the sink, please use a step stool made and rated for children. If it helps, I could build something safe that doesn't hold any weight: a caddy for the bathroom counter with a holder for your toddler's toothbrush and cup and bins for the toothpaste and soap. You could put it low or close to the sink so it's easier for them to reach.
